llm.title: Language model (optional)
llm.description: Jev decides every command and query on its own. A language model is only used to split requests that contain several commands, and to answer general questions. Leave this blank to skip it.

native.title: Decision provider
native.description: Use an OpenRouter key for pinned Jev 1.13, or a TypeSafe key from {console_url}. New agents default to preview mode. Disable local handling in the Assist pipeline when testing preview mode.

data.execution_enabled: Allow device commands (off means preview only)

quickstart.title: Quick start without YAML
quickstart.description: Ready-made profile: JEV 1.13 + GPT-4o mini, spending limits, Assist-exposed lights and numeric sensors. Choose an existing OpenRouter entry (leave the key blank) or select New API key and enter a key. Commands default to off; enable permission for control. After setup, select this agent in Assist and expose the desired entities. Internet search is off. [Setup guide]({docs_url}).

data_description.always_confirm_risky: Ask first before unlocking a door, opening a garage or disarming an alarm, however sure the model is. Turning this off lets confident requests through silently.
data_description.inline_entity_descriptions: Costs roughly twice the tokens. Only worth turning on if the agent picks the wrong device.
data_description.bypass_local_intents: By default Home Assistant's own sentence matcher keeps the phrasings it recognises, and only sends the rest here. Turn this on to send everything here instead.

scope.title: Basic profile entity scope
scope.description: Empty list: all Assist-exposed lights and numeric sensors (up to 100). Nonempty list: only selected entities that are also exposed to Assist. This never exposes hidden entities. Room commands affect the selected lights in that area; select only the desired fixtures if you want primary lighting.

help.title: Getting started
help.description:
1. For a new home: add the integration → Quick start: lights and sensors, then choose your OpenRouter credential source.
2. In voice assistant settings, expose the desired lights and numeric sensors. Assign clear names, aliases and areas.
3. Select the TypeSafe agent in your Assist pipeline. Disable preferred local HA command handling when testing this agent specifically.
4. Enable device permission in Safety and agent. Until then commands are planned only.
5. Optionally restrict the Lights and sensors entity scope. Models and limits are preselected; review their settings.

Try: turn on the room light, make this lamp slightly brighter, or what is the room temperature? History needs Recorder data. Music, cleaning and custom workflows require the advanced profile; no household-specific mappings are bundled.

[Complete setup guide and limitations]({docs_url}).
